Name these mathematical objects in which n2 numbers are arranged such that the n numbers in all the rows, columns, and main diagonals have the same sum.

This man derisively called the United Nations "the thingamabob" in criticism of its handling of the Congo Crisis and refused to contribute to peacekeeping efforts. This man was placated with the Luxembourg Compromise after he boycotted the Council of the European Union during a dispute over the Common Agricultural Policy. This leader cut a visit to Canada short after Pierre Trudeau asked him about the acceptability of a Canadian Prime leader supporting Breton nationalists; Trudeau's question was a response to a controversial speech by this leader during Montreal's Expo 67 in which he voiced support for a free Quebec. His tenure saw the signing of the Evian Accords and student and worker riots in May 1968. Earlier, he gained emergency power following the Algerian Crisis. Name this first president of the France's Fifth Republic, the leader of the Free French during World War II.
Charles André Joseph Marie de Gaulle

Khalid al-Walid's forces did not destroy this city because the Byzantine Thomas surrendered to another general at one gate while Khalid's forces rushed in from another gate. One theologian from this city wrote a seminal work which summarized Christian theology until then in the "Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith." A monk named John from this city defended the use of icons. Its most famous mosque was ordered to be constructed by Al-Walid I, but was burned by Tamerlane when he conquered this city. The Council of Acre decided to attack this city, which was allied to Jerusalem during the Second Crusade. Muawiya made this city the capital of the expanding Umayyad Caliphate. Name this Syrian city, its capital.

Soon after ascending to the throne, this ruler executed the horribly incompetent General Ramorino, who had earlier gambled away money meant to raise an army in Paris that could aid rebels against this ruler's father. Early on, this ruler was served by Prime Minister Massimo d'Azeglio and he married his cousin Adelaide of Austria. Early in his reign, he put down a revolt in Genoa. His son and successor approved of a massacre of strikers protesting the government of Antonio Rudini by General Bava-Beccaris. This ruler's morganic wife Rosa Vercellana was born to a Napoleonic soldier and he was excommunicated by Pius IX. His minister famously asked for Napoleon III's aid at Plombieres. His capital was originally at Turin and this "Father of the Fatherland" was ably served by Count Cavour. Name this ruler during the risorgiomento, the first Italian king.

This man renamed a city after Mount Qishan, where the Chinese Zhou dynasty had supposedly been founded. This man renamed the city of Gifu and destroyed a group of Jodo Shinshu followers after a long siege. In one battle, with less than 10% of the enemy troops, he defeated a rival through a gorge ambush. His philosophy has been described by the line "If the bird does not sing, kill it!" This victor at Okehazama was forced by Akechi Mitsuhide to commit suicide. He brought down the Ashikaga Shogunate. Name this first unifier of Japan who was succeeded by Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu.

One leader of this province became embroiled in a scandal when he certified thousands of orphans as mentally ill because insane asylums were funded by the federal government. Antonio Cordasco had himself honored by a 4,000 man parade in this province whose town of Rimouski was the main site where survivors of the wreck of the Empress of Ireland nautical disaster were sent. The Carignan-Salieres Regiment established a series of fortifications in this province that saw two conscription crises occur during the two world wars. Maurice Duplessis and Henri Bourassa were premiers of this province in which the Quiet Revolution occurred. Pierre Laporte's murder touched off a series of terrorist attacks conducted by the FLQ in its October Crisis. Name this Francophone Canadian province home to the city of Montreal.

One bill vetoed by this man would have used earning bonuses from one entity to create a federal highway and was known as the Bonus Bill. A spy named John Henry was paid fifty thousand dollars by this president for information that he reported to James Craig concerning the possibility of New England defecting to Canada. During his presidency, the term "Blue Light" was applied to British sympathizers, and a successor to the Non-Intercourse Act called Macon's Bill No. 2 was passed. In one essay, this man claimed that the creation of a Republic will limit the power of factions. His presidency saw Tecumseh's death and William Henry Harrison's victory at the Battle of the Thames. This author of Federalist no. 10 saw the end of a major conflict with the signing of the Treaty of Ghent. Name this president during the War of 1812 who also authored the Bill of Rights.

During this conflict, Rohrbach forced Duke Helfenstein and his company to run the gauntlet in an event termed the Weinsberger Blood Vengeance. Florian Geyer led a heavy cavalry unit called the "Black Company" during this conflict. This war inspired Michael Gaismayr to draw up a new Territorial Constitution in Tyrol. One side in this conflict demanded to abolishment of the Todfall, an inheritance tax, as part of their Twelve Articles. One leader dubbed himself the "sword of Gideon" and his use of Biblical language was analyzed by Engels. The battle of Frankenhausen saw the defeat of Thomas Munzer's forces decimated by Philip of Hesse. It was partly sparked by the teachings of Martin Luther, who decried its instigators as "Murderous, Thieving Hordes." name this 1524 uprising of the lower classes in the Holy Roman Empire.

In Scotland, one leader of these people was Johnnie Faa, who was supposedly hung for eloping with Lady Cassilis. King Ferdinand VI authorized a "Great Roundup" of these people in Spain in 1749. Among these people, problems are settled in a court called the Kris. Those who do not belong to this group are called gadje. In the 20th century, these people were the targets of the Porajnos. Frequent invasions by Mahmud of Ghazni may have caused these people to leave their ancestral land in India. Name these nomadic people, who are also called "Roma."

During this conflict, the Gongota Agreement ended an intervention that tried to evacuate an army that had seized large parts of a major railroad with armored trains. One party in this conflict was led by a Central Rada, which was replaced by a Hetmanate. Nestor Makhno's anarchist Makhnovshchina, or Black Army, prevented the capture of one side's capital in this conflict by attacking the forces of Anton Denikin. Advancement of the Czechoslovak Legions during this conflict resulted in the execution of a former ruler in Yekaterinburg. The Kronstadt Rebellion resulted from the policy of war communism in this conflict; that policy had been implemented to supply an army led by Leon Trotsky. Name this war between the Reds and Whites following the October Revolution.

The only banner to have survived this event stated "Unity and Strength" and was carried by Thomas Redford. One act passed in response to this event forbade the meeting of 50 or more men to discuss matters of "church or state" without a magistrate's or sheriff's permission. The Seditious Meetings Act was passed in response to it and Hugh Birley may have been drunk during this event. This event led to an assassination plot by Arthur Thistlewood against the British cabinet at Lord Harrowby's house. In addition to prompting the failed Cato Street Conspiracy, this event led Robert Jenkinson, the Prime Minister during this event, to pass the Six Acts. This event proceeded the Spa Field riots and was named for the Duke of Wellington's victory at Waterloo. Name this British massacre of people who were gathered to listen to Henry Hunt.

One pope of this name increased papal control of the French church by convincing Louis XI to repeal the Pragmatic Sanction of Bourges. That pope, the second of this name, also wrote a novel called The Tale of Two Lovers. Another pope of this name issued the only encyclical ever written in German, Mit brennender Sorge, to condemn Nazism, and an earlier pope of this name established as dogma the immaculate conception of the Virgin Mary. Give the name shared by these popes, the eleventh of whom gave up claims to the Papal States but secured the sovereignty of Vatican City in the Lateran Pact and the ninth and longest serving of whom defined the doctrine of papal infallibility.

Vichy defense minister Maxime Weygand may have been the illegitimate child of this man's widow. He had originally been slated to marry Maria Amalia of Braganza, but she died before they could be united. After an assassination attempt on his brother, this man rallied for the construction of the Votive Church in his homeland. He disastrously implemented the Black Decree, calling for the execution of enemy prisoners. This man was shown fraudulent voting statistics that said his reign was popular. The husband of Carlota of Belgium, he was executed after he was captured in the province of Queretaro by Benito Juarez. Name this Austrian who, at the urging of Napoleon III, became king of Mexico.

People who did not follow this legislation had their outputs taxed at a rate of 50%, and its implementation was overseen by Chester Davis. Certain provisions in this legislation's successor were declared constitutional in the Supreme Court cases of Mulford v. Smith and Wickard v. Filburn. This legislation contained a bill named after an Oklahoma senator that greatly expanded the president's power to control monetary policy. The Thomas Amendment was attached as Title III to this legislation that Owen Roberts decided violated the tenth amendment by controlling powers that should be left to the states in the Supreme Court case of Bulter v. U.S. This legislation provided payments to farmers who limited production of crops. Name this 1933 New Deal Legislation.

The Twelve Apostles were a special operations arm of this group and once targeted the Cairo Gang. This group burned the Custom House with heavy casualties in an attempt to destabilize their enemy's administration. Their opponents committed atrocities such as the slaughter of civilians spectating a soccer game while fighting this group not based in Russia that partially caused a Bloody Sunday. They fought the Blacks and Tans and Roger Casement supplied the weapons for the uprising that eventually resulted in Michael Collins leading this group. They achieved peace with their primary foe in 1922 and earlier became the military arm of the organization formed following the Easter Uprising, Sinn Féin. Name this army that fought the British for independence of a nearby Gaelic island.

One building built in honor of this man has an eastern relief in which two goddesses, riding a sea serpent and a swan, flank a personification of Tellus. In one sculpture of this man, a cupid is riding on a vertically-oriented dolphin next to his right leg. In that sculpture, he holds a baton in his right hand and wears a breastplate ornamented with a sphinx on each shoulder and other gods representing his accomplishments. The Ara Pacis was built to honor this man's achievements, while a famous marble statue of this man was found at Prima Porta. A building built during this man's reign is located in the south of the Piazza della Rotonda and contains a large oculus at the top to let in light. Name this emperor who presided over the building of the Pantheon, the first emperor of Rome.

One ruler of this state was bribed by the Byzantines to invade Bulgaria, won the battle of Silistra, and even besieged Adrianople before being forced to evacuate all of Bulgaria by Emperor John Tzimiskes. Many cities that formed this state had a popular assembly called the veche. Its first ruler was Oleg, while the previously described ruler was Sviatoslav. This state's most famous ruler rejected Islam, because it prohibited drinking alcohol, and Judaism, as he felt that the Jews had been abandoned by God. That man was married to Anna Porphyrogeneta, the sister of Basil II, and was awed by the Hagia Sophia. While one of his sons was known as the Wise, and this state converted to Christianity under Vladimir the Great. Name this medieval Russian state centered at the modern day capital of Ukraine.

One argument in this trial attempted to refute that an action went against the laws of god by quoting Paul in Acts that "I wish not, brethren, that he was the high priest" and by quoting from Peter to despise a certain group of people for "Presumptuous are they, self-willed, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities." The defense in this trial drew up a comparison between the punishments handed out to Brewster and Doctor Sacheverell because they were committed at different points in time after likening the prosecution and the judges to a star chamber. The defendant was represented by Andrew Hamilton after Hamilton was informed of his situation by Ben Franklin, and the prosecution was sparred on by passages in the New York Journal attacking governor William Cosby. Name this 1735 trial of a printer that established some notion of freedom of the press.

In On Modesty, Tertullian ironically gives Pope Calixtus I this title for issuing an edict that removed the repentance needed for adultery. This title's holder held the secespita and the Lex Domitia allowed the people to elect the members of the group that elected one of their own to hold this title. It was first established by Numa Pompilius and the Lex Ogulnia increased that group to 9. This title's holder oversaw the flamines, lived in the Domus Publica, and was forbidden to leave Italy, though Julius Caesar ignored that prohibition. Gratian was the last emperor to hold this title and the popes eventually assumed this former imperial title. People holding this position were responsible for regulating the calendar, maintaining pax decorum or peace of the gods, and watching over the Vestal Virgins. Name this head of the Roman state religion.

One side at this battle had their cavalry commanded by Mirabeau Lamar, who had been promoted the day before due to his valiance in combat. One participant, nicknamed "deaf," learned from two prisoners of enemy troop movements, leading Erasmus Smith to destroy Vince's Bridge after it was crossed by Martin Cos. Followed by the "public" and "secret" treaties of Velasco, one side used a cannon known as the Twin Sisters. The losing commander attempted to escape by clothing himself as a regular soldier, but he was captured and recognized by his own men. This battle lasted barely twenty minutes as one side was caught gathering wood and taking a siesta. Name this battle at which cries of "Remember the Alamo" enabled Sam Houston's troops to secure the independence of Texas from Mexico.

Great Britain's response to one invasion of this country was polled for by the Peace Ballot. One leader of this country failed to replace the Maria Theresa thaler and became king of this country following the Battle of Gallabat. This country fought the battle of Debenguina during its Christmas Offensive in response to an invasion prompted by the Walwal incident. One leader of this country succeeded Yohannes IV and signed the Treaty of Wuchale, before winning the Battle of Adowa. Italy's second invasion of this country prompted its leader to appeal to the League of Nations. Name this African country formerly led by Menelik II and Halie Salessie, with capital at Addis Ababa.

One battle in this war saw one side weakened when their animals were led to Fort Craig after they stampeded in search of water. Another battle in this war included John Chivington's raid on enemy supplies at Johnson's Ranch and begun when Charles Pyron attacked from his camp in Apache Canyon. Those battles at Valverde and Glorieta Pass preceded Henry Sibley's retreat from Santa Fe and Albuquerque in this war's western theater. A controversy during this war erupted after the seizure of diplomats James Mason and James Slidell. One side in this war employed Samuel Du Pont in an attempt to blockade its enemy's ports that also included the capture of Fernandina in Florida; proposed by Winfield Scott, that effort was termed the Anaconda Plan. Name this war that led to the downfall of the Confederate States of America.

The Hundred Regiments offensive was led by this man's subordinates Péng Déhuái and Zhū Dé. Liú Shàoqí opposed one of this man's policies, but Lín Biāo defended this man's ideas, leading Lín to be considered this man's heir. This man's strategies were used over Otto Braun's strategies after the Zūnyì conference. However, this husband of Jiāng Qīng's suspicions eventually led Lín to die while attempting to escape via airplane. The Dixie Mission concluded that this man would be a good ally after being stationed at his base at Yán'ān. Originally a peasant from Húnán, he led the Long March. This leader's attempts to modernize his country led to a Great Famine from 1958 to 1961 after instating backyard furnaces in the Great Leap Forward. Name this first Chinese Communist leader.

The instigators of this event were surprised when their first action, a sneak attack on a weapons arsenal, was foiled because the mistress of Henry Gladwin, their target's commander, had warned the defenders of their violent intentions. It included battles at Bushy and Bloody Runs as well as the Devil's Hole Massacre. Lazarus Stewart led a group in response to this event that promulgated a "Remonstrance of Distressed and Bleeding Frontier Inhabitants" after its march on Philadelphia was defused partially by Benjamin Franklin. Its siege of Fort Pitt was countered by an attempt to spread smallpox among its instigators, and it had earlier failed to capture Fort Detroit. Name this Native American insurrection that prompted the formation of the Paxton Boys and was organized by its namesake leader in 1763.

In one battle, Ralph of Tesson rejoined this man's forces to help defeat the forces of this man's cousin Guy of Burgundy. In addition to the victory chronicled by William of Malmesbury of this man and his liege Henry I at the Battle of Val-es-Dunes, he slaughtered thousands and burned all the crops, causing thousands more to die of starvation, after Edgar Aetheling invaded with assistance from the Danes and Scots. He dealt with the rebellion of Hereward the Wake and with the Harrying of the North. His most famous victory is chronicled in a tapestry made by his half-brother Odo. That victory was won after his enemy was shot in the eye by an arrow following intense fighting around a housecarl shield wall with repeated cavalry charges. Ordering a census for his new lands, name this ruler who compiled the Domesday Book, a Norman that defeated Harold Godwinson at Hastings.

One treasure of this empire was an umbrella called "katamanso," which translates as "The covering of the nation." This empire's family system of Abusua shows that all members can trace their lineage back to one of seven people. This state absorbed its predecessor, Denkyira, after Osei Tutu led a successful rebellion. One late queen of this empire was Yaa Asantewaa, who was exiled to the Seychelles after her defeat. The Pra River was proclaimed a boundary of this empire after a conflict in which they defeated and killed a force led by Charles McCarthy near their capital of Kumasi, though they were later subjugated by Garnet Wolseley. Name this West African empire that fought a series of namesake wars against the British during the 19th Century and revered the Golden Stool.

Willigis was an important minister for this dynasty, serving during the reigns of three rulers. This dynasty sponsored the abbey of Quedlinburg founded by Matilda of Ringelheim, the wife of its first ruler. Although it was not French, one of its rulers defeated a revolt named the War of the Three Henries. The fourth ruler of this dynasty met Boleslaw the Brave at the Council of Gniezno and was a student of Gerbert of Aurillac or Sylvester II. That son of the Byzantine princess Theophanu was succeeded by Henry the Saint. The second ruler of this dynasty married Adelaide of Italy to gain Lombardy, and gave land to bishops to ensure their loyalty as part of a state church. He defeated the Magyars at Lechfeld, began a namesake Renaissance, and was the son of Henry the Fowler. Name this dynasty of the first Holy Roman Emperors.

During one siege of this city, its ruler, who was fond of dancing mockingly on its walls, sent out peace delegations that extolled the wonders of this city instead of negotiating. The death of one of this city's commanders was kept secret for 30 days until after a victory off of Cyprus. The Peace of Callias earned by this city was contrasted with the King's Peace signed after Persia withdrew support for this city during the Corinthian War. This city's government was overthrown by the coup of the Four Hundred. This city, which started the Lamian War against Antipater, included Phocion the Good and Aristides the Just among its statesman. In another war, this city's navy was defeated by Lysander at Aegospotami and Alcibiades betrayed its expedition to Sicily. Name this Attican city, the loser in the Peloponnesian war where Cleisthenes started Greek democracy.

One text outlining this organization's goals is the Odd Fellows Improved Manual, written by Aaron Grosh. Susan B. Anthony gave her last public speech at a meeting of this organization, which was founded partly by Caroline A Hall. This organization is divided into Subordinate, Pomona, State, and National levels. Membership in this organization was organized into seven degrees, with the seventh being High Priest of Demeter. This organization was one of the main creators of the Greenback Party. It was founded by a man ordered to tour the south by Andrew Johnson; that was Oliver Hazard Kelley. This organization was vindicated in the case Munn v. Illinois, which allowed the government to regulate grain elevators. Name this rural advocacy group that agitated for namesake laws regulating railroad freight rates.
The National Grange of the Order of Patrons of Husbandry

After a letter sent to this ruler by Tewodros II was misplaced, the Ethiopian emperor felt insulted and imprisoned several people in the Magdala fort. This ruler fought with the Royal Household to ensure the rights of a rumored member of the Muslim Patriotic League, the Munshi Abdul Karim. This ruler hated being brought up in the Kensington System of Sir John Conroy, whose supposed impregnation of Flora Hastings led to the latter's dismissal during the reign of this ruler. This monarch's first Prime Minister, Lord Melbourne, was reinstated after a plan to replace Whig ladies-in-waiting by Robert Peel failed during the Bedchamber Crisis. This monarch's spouse organized the Crystal Palace Great Exhibition. Name this last ruler of the House of Hanover, an Empress of India and longest ruling British monarch.

Members of one ethnic group fleeing from this country have often crossed the Naf River into the town of Cox's Bazaar, but recently international human rights organizations have been banned from operating there. This nation's Kachin state has been the side of long-standing tensions with the Christian Karen minority, who were favored by British colonists. This nation's leadership was criticized when initially failing to accept relief aid after the deadly Cyclone Nargis in 2008. The 8888 uprising in this nation led to the repression of the National League for Democracy, and in June 2012 this nation's state of Rakhine was the site of armed conflicts with the Islamic Rohingya people, the relocation of whom was suggested by this nation's president Thein Sein. Identify this Asian nation whose ruling military junta has often been opposed by Aung San Suu Kyi.

The last ruler of this dynasty had presided over a massacre in the capital to kill the supporters of its penultimate ruler, and would go on to marry a daughter of Louis VII of France. The second ruler of this dynasty may have shot down the succession hopes of his eldest son in order to follow in the AIMA prophecy. The founder of this dynasty signed the Treaty of Devol to gain the homage of the ruler of Antioch and had used an alliance with the Cumans to defeat the Pechenegs. The marriage of this dynasty's founder to Irene cemented its relationship with the Doukas family after succeeding Nikephorus III Botaneites. Another ruler of this dynasty applied oaths of fealty to men he had received after appealing to the Council of Clermont to begin the First Crusade. Name this Byzantine dynasty of John II, Manuel, and Alexius I.

One count of this region killed his brother-in-law Vermudo III at the Battle of Tamaron. One army from this region was routed at the Battle of Alarcos. One ruler of this region enlisted the help of Edward the Black Prince at the Battle of Najera and defeated his half-brother Henry Trastamara to regain the throne. That ruler fought Peter IV in the "War of the Two Peters." This region was home to Peter the Cruel, and a succession crisis in this region included the Battle of Toro and concluded with the Treaty of Alcacovas. That crisis was brought about after Afonso V claimed the throne of this place, accusing queen Joan of having an affair. Another ruler of this region came to power with the death of Henry IV and was the daughter of John II. Name this region of central Spain which was united with Aragon by the wedding of Ferdinand and Isabella.

One article stated that one participant in this event arrived on a "jet-clipper armada". Winston Lord was cropped out of several photographs taken during it, and Max Frankel won a Pulitzer for his coverage of it. One communique released during this event, a prime example of "constructive ambiguity", outlined an opposition to "hegemony and power politics". One participant in these events outlined what were later called his namesake "Five Principles". One politician called this event the "Week that changed the world", and that figure was accompanied by William Rogers. This event was facilitated by an exchange in which Tim Boggan and ten other table tennis players participated. It was organized through a series of secret meetings held by Henry Kissinger. Name this event in which the president of the United States flew to a nation headed by Mao Zedong.

During one battle, this war's victors dug shallow trenches in rocky ground only for the fog to lift and show that they were not on the summit of Spy Hill; that became known as the "acre of massacre." The mutilation of Captain Hunt in this war led to the summary execution of prisoners by Breaker Morant. In this war, the successor of Lord Roberts used barbed wire and blockhouses to make grids, which were subsequently depopulated. That practice was criticized by the Fawcett Commission. The first major overseas deployment of Canadian and New Zealand troops was in this war. The victors suffered a Black Week while trying to relieve the siege of Mafeking and Ladysmith. Name this war in which Lord Kitchener used concentration camps to house some Afrikaner farmers.

One section of this work states that preserving the nation requires discounting "irregular oppositions" and resisting the spirit of innovations, and another states that "institutions for the general diffusion of knowledge" are vital. Another section says that "the Palladium of your political safety" is the Union. Another section of it foreshadows a later speech by stating that "overgrown military establishments" are hostile to liberty in any government system. This speech, which is read every year on February 22nd in Congress, uses the phrase "frightful despotism" to describe the alternating domination of political parties and warned against permanent alliances with foreign nations. Name this letter written by the first President of the United States immediately before leaving office.

One member of this dynasty names an unhygienic building that was used to elect Pope Celestine IV who fell sick and died since the urine of the guards on the roof leaked onto the cardinals. This dynasty's founder told his sons to "get along, enrich the army, and despise everyone else." This dynasty includes the ruler who granted Roman citizenship to all residents of the empire. One ruler of this dynasty introduced the cult of Sol Invictus and married a Vestal Virgin. This dynasty's founder claimed to be supporting Pertinax when he beheaded an emperor who won a Praetorian auction, Didius Julianus, after which he defeated Pescennius Niger and Clodius Albinus to end the Year of the Five Emperors. Name this Roman dynasty of Elagabalus, Geta, and Caracalla that was started by an African general named Septimius.

This politician's abode was bombed by a pair of A-1 Skyraiders in one coup attempt. His government often made use of Decree Number 10, which outlawed certain flags. This president's army poured liquid tear gas on protesters in one incident, and his government's secret police force assaulted journalists on Double Seven Day. Cable 243 was sent by ambassador Henry Cabot Lodge, Jr. After this man ordered a raid on the Xa Loi Pagoda. This man's sister-in-law made a comment about barbecues after seeing a monk immolate himself in protest against this man's regime. Name this Catholic politician assassinated after a series of mass Buddhist protests, the first president of South Vietnam.

One party that advocated this cause elected Reinhold Sadler as governor of Nevada. Cuba-related amendment namesake Henry Moore Teller founded a political party named for this cause, which also included a senator from Idaho who was obsessed with disenfranchising Mormons, named Fred Dubois. Supporters of this cause attempted to force the passage of the Matthews resolution. One statement in favor of this cause stated that the controversy over it was "the issue of 1776 all over again". Proponents of this cause advocated a certain 16 to 1 ratio. This cause, which was heavily favored by indebted farmers and galvanized by the "Crime of '73", was advanced by the Bland-Allison act and a law named for Sherman. Name this cause advanced by William Jennings Bryan in the "Cross of Gold" speech, calling for the use of a certain metal in coinage.

The work Commentariorum linguae Latinae was dedicated to this king by Etienne Dolet, who was rumored to be his bastard son. This king created the first legal deposit system with his Ordonnance de Montpellier and put Guillaume Bude in charge of his Royal Library. Originally tolerant of Protestants, he began persecuting them after finding anti-Catholic posters at his door in the Affair of the Placards. The English fought this man in the Four Years' War after he failed to forge an alliance with them at the Field of the Cloth of Gold. In a later Italian War, Hayreddin Barbarossa's Ottoman navy helped him gain victory during the Siege of Nice against the allies of his archrival Charles V. Name this French Renaissance monarch who ordered the construction of the French castle of Fontainebleau, received the last breath of Leonardo da Vinci, and was beaten at the Battle of Pavia.

British general Alfred Knox was a witness to an important military action during this event. During this event, a crisis over the control of the Aland Islands was resolved by the League of Nations. American writer Louise Bryant also witnessed this event, and this event saw the mobilization of Women's Battalions to guard a critical site. This event was chronicled in the book Ten Days That Shook the World by John Reed, and an attempted coup by Lavr Kornilov was averted during this event. A blank shot fired by the crew of the Aurora triggered the attack that completed this event. The group behind this event had been weakened after Alexander Kerensky cracked down on them during the July Days. Name this 1917 event during which a certain group of communists took control of the Winter Palace, St. Petersburg, and eventually all of Russia.

Daniel De Leon argued that this organization had been taken over by "the bummery" before he formed a splinter group. This organization used stickers called "Silent Agitators," to spread its messages, and its charter states that "we must inscribe on our banner the revolutionary watchword, 'Abolition of the wage system.'" The motto of this organization was "An injury to one is an injury to all," and this organization was outraged when Frank Little was lynched in Montana. "Songs to fan the flame of discontent" was the subtitle of little red song books carried by members of this organization. It was formed by a coalition that included Thomas Hagerty, Big Bill Haywood, and Eugene Debs in opposition to trade unionism in the American Federation of Labor. Name this labor union affectionately known as the "Wobblies."

This was the name of an anti-Prussian party led by Ludwig Windthorst. This was the name of a legion that was sponsored from 1866-1870 by a blind George V to try and regain lost lands and territories. The only Holy Roman Emperor from a house of this name was excommunicated by Innocent III for trying to conquer Sicily from his future successor, Frederick II; that member of this house was Otto IV. This house under Henry the Lion was defeated by Frederick Barbarossa and lost its ancient duchies of Saxony and Bavaria. Since this house were the electors of Hanover that frequently challenged Hohenstaufen power, this word also applies to a group that supported the Pope in opposition to the Holy Roman Emperor. Name this word that names a group opposed to the Ghibellines.

This ruler allowed port cities to keep legal fees in court cases in exchange for naval defense when needed in the arrangement of "Cinque Ports." This ruler was constantly in the service of the earls Siward and Leofric, and he increased his number of Norman advisors, angering the Witan. During this man's reign the citizens of Dover rioted against Eustace of Boulogne, partially in response to this man's appointment of Robert of Jumieges as Archbishop of Canterbury, which angered his father in law Godwin. His intended successor was the ill-fated Edgar Aethling, the son of his brother Edmund Ironside. This ruler was the son of Emma of Normandy and Aethelred the Unready, and he either promised the throne to Harold or William. Name this Anglo-Saxon king who first constructed Westminster Abbey and who was canonized as a saint.
